Rationale Summary description and rationale of proposed specialization.
Program Context: The TESOL/BDL program allowed undergraduates to earn their ESOL or BDL certification as part of their undergraduate experience between 2018-2024.
In 2023-2024,the State added certification requirements to undergraduate programs, such as Right to Read Legislation and a year-long teaching residency, making it too difficult for students to add a full certification (21 credits) to their undergraduate program.
As a result, TESOl/BDL faculty have been encouraging undergraduates to it did not allow for double counting of credits and it required students to pay a Graduate School application fee.
Adding an ABM would formalize a pathway for undergraduate students to complete two certification and earn two degrees in five years.
Out of state undergraduate students would benefit from the ABM pathway because many states (excluding Rl) require educators to earn a masters degree within five years of employment (e.g., Connecticut, Massachusetts, New York).

Additional State-wide Context: the Regulations specifies that educators in Rhode Island schools must demonstrate"proficiency or awareness" in Multilingual Learner (MLL) education.
Proficiency and awareness were defined by The Rhode Island Department of Education in September 2025, with the release of their MLL Competencies.
These regulatory changes have reduced the demand for educators to earn their full teaching certification through UR's M.A. in TESOL/BDL program.
As a result, TESOL/BDL faculty are proposing changes to the existing courses and program to meet the State's"proficiency" requirements and retain enrollment through a variety of pathways:Graduate Certificate,Accelerated Bachelors to Certificate (ABC), and Accelerated Bachelors to Masters (ABM).
Important for Reviewers to Note: students to take two additional courses in the fall/spring semesters of their senior year.
The proposers understand that students cannot officially apply to the ABM until they have earned a minimum of 90 credits.
The ABM specialization goals are the same as for the MA in TESOL/BDL program.
